# Best noise-cancelling headphones under $200

I can't browse, so I'm working from the search results. Prices change often, so check the current price before you buy.

## My top picks

**1. Best ANC: JBL Live 780NC**
- RTINGS ranks it the best noise-cancelling pair under $200. Its ANC competes with Sony and Bose flagships.
- It has 60 hours of battery, multipoint, and LDAC.
- It clamps fairly hard and the headband padding is thin, so it may be uncomfortable for larger heads.
- RTINGS says it sometimes goes on sale just below the $200 cutoff, so it may cost more at times.
- Review, with retailer price buttons: https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/noise-cancelling-headphones-under-200

**2. Best value: Soundcore Space One (about $100)**
- It supports LDAC (Android only), has adjustable ANC and 3.5 mm input, and lasts about 43 hours with ANC on, per SoundGuys via [RatingMobile](https://ratingmobile.com/articles/en/best-noise-cancelling-headphones-under-200).
- Dealectric lists it at $99.99, or $80 with code AFSC20, which was tested in Soundcore's cart on 2026-10-22. The code doesn't apply to items already on sale.
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-space-one. This is an affiliate link that opens Soundcore's official store, and Dealectric earns a commission.
- RTINGS' budget pick is the related Soundcore Space Q45, which costs about $100. It has strong noise isolation and about 28 hours of battery. RTINGS notes some hiss and user reports of hinge or headband breakage. Review: https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/budget-noise-cancelling-headphones

**3. Best sound: Sennheiser Accentum Plus**
- It has a smooth, bass-forward sound, a parametric EQ, and 56 hours of battery.
- Its ANC is weaker than the JBL's and Anker's, especially on low rumble like plane engines.
- It has no headband padding, and Apple devices don't support aptX Adaptive.
- Review: https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/by-price/under-200

**4. Best for calls and all-around use: Sony ULT WEAR (about $200)**
- RTINGS picks it for calls. SoundGuys measured over 25 dB of attenuation above 80 Hz and found it comfortable, with multipoint and LDAC ([RatingMobile](https://ratingmobile.com/articles/en/best-noise-cancelling-headphones-under-200)).
- It sits right at the price cap.
- RTINGS review: https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/noise-cancelling-headphones-under-200

## Other options
- **Cheapest decent option:** The JLab JBuds Lux ANC costs about $80 and has a long battery life. Its ANC is the weakest of the group, at 10–20 dB below 700 Hz, so it only takes the edge off a bus or office ([RatingMobile](https://ratingmobile.com/articles/en/best-noise-cancelling-headphones-under-200)).
- **Sony WH-CH730N:** It's comfortable, with good ANC and sound, but Tom's Guide thinks the US price of about $176–179 is too high ([review](https://www.tomsguide.com/audio/headphones/sony-wh-ch730n-review)).
- **Soundcore Space One Pro:** It's $199.99, or $160 with AFSC20, and Tom's Guide names it best under $200. Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-space-one-pro

## Quick advice
- Pick the **JBL Live 780NC** if you want the strongest noise cancelling.
- Pick the **Soundcore Space One** if you want the best deal.
- Pick the **Sennheiser Accentum Plus** if sound quality matters most.

For the JBL, Sennheiser, and Sony, I only have review pages, not direct retailer links. The retailer buttons on those RTINGS pages go to Amazon, Best Buy, and others.
